svg.title: Simple Boston Whaler Conquest hull: buses, plant, gated actuators, and docking approach
svg.desc: Simpler follow-on for the live seagoing test bench. Left: same stern-first Boston Whaler Conquest outline with dual Raymarine Axiom+ 9 and VesselView on SeaTalk NG (Yacht Devices listen, working; YDEN-03 ordered as the boat adapter), a parallel later NMEA OneNet PoE++ Ethernet (48 V from a 12→48 V step-up in the cluster) to cameras, ranging, bow IR, and radar; solar is 12 V house top-off, not PoE++, gated actuator requests to the twin 300 hp Mercurys (later), and 12 V from alternators plus Kohler or later LiFePO4. Helm interface is SeaTalk NG only. Right: smaller slip with the boat still outside, stern-first on a diagonal planned track under wind and current. Dashboard only. Not a helm. Not a write path.
svg.text: Live seagoing test bench. SeaTalk NG and OneNet PoE++ run stern to bow as equal backbones.
0183 sensors ride N2K via converter. Stern up.
not NET-S · not the helm · not claimed
0183 joins N2K through a converter T-drop. VHF still takes Axiom+ 0183 OUT.
Cyan = SeaTalk NG. Teal = OneNet PoE++. Parallel equal backbones. Amber = 0183 into the converter.
If scoped: fused T, YDEN-03 (ordered), Ethernet, 12 V main computer. Dual 30 A stay.
Later: OneNet PoE++ cameras, ranging, bow IR, radar, edge computer. Solar is 12 V top-off.
Extra display is not an Axiom+. MCP and the pilot gate are software in the cluster.

g.text: current - out from under dock, pushes stern out of slip

svg.text: Reads stored SignalK. Not on ingest. Not a helm.
Pilot in command at every rung. Override does not need this box.
Orange is gated thrust. Supervised self-docking is last, and not unattended.
Two equal backbones. Helm and control on SeaTalk NG. Data-rich sensors on OneNet.
